manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 5 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a short broadcast message (at most 100 words). It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <your message to your teammates>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm moving A up toward its goal at (R2,C3). Could someone move their object out of (R2,C3)? I'll need that cell free in a few turns.
move: A up

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.


CURRENT BOARD:
Objects: A@R5C7 X@R5C8 X@R7C8 X@R3C1 X@R1C2 X@R8C7
Walls: R1C1 R2C1 R2C4 R3C3 R4C2 R4C5 R4C6 R4C7 R4C8 R5C2 R6C3 R6C5 R6C6 R6C7 R6C8 R7C1 R7C3 R8C1

GOAL BOARD (where each object must end up):
Targets: A->R5C8

- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5.
